clauses.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11436 Suspending provisions of section 6372 of title 10, U.S.C., relating to retirement or retention on the" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.
clauses.reason: whole: The order's sole operative sentence suspends the cited provisions of title 10 of the United States Code. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11436 Suspending provisions of section 6372 of title 10, U.S.C., relating to retirement or retention on the"). The order states no duration, so no own-terms end applies. Earlier candidate ends that do not name this order, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; none is the end because none names EO 11436): the Defense Officer Personnel Management Act, Pub. L. 96-513 (Dec. 12, 1980), repealed chapter 545 (section 333, which includes section 5701) and sections 6371 and 6372 and 6386 of chapter 573 (section 335), effective September 15, 1981 under section 701(a) (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11436_Defense_Officer_Personnel_Management_Act_Pub._L._96-513_Dec._12_1980_94_Stat._2835_in_bdcccb89ac.txt). Section 702 of that Act preserves the suspended status of a provision that is amended, not repealed. I did not establish that the repeal extinguished this order's suspension, and the pre-1981 text of 10 U.S.C. 5711(b) and 6386(c), which the order cites as its authority, is not held, so no statutory duration limit on the suspension is shown either way.

research_rationale:
EO 11436 (1968-12-02, 33 FR 17943) suspends section 6372 of title 10, United States Code (retirement or retention on the active list of certain rear admirals in the Navy), citing section 6386(c) of that title. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11436.txt, 33 FR 17943, PDF pages 7-7); its single operative sentence is the whole order, and it states no duration. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes it by number. The first end is that express revocation. Section 702 of that Act preserves the suspended status of a provision that is amended, not repealed. I did not establish that the repeal extinguished this order's suspension, and the pre-1981 text of 10 U.S.C. 5711(b) and 6386(c), which the order cites as its authority, is not held, so no statutory duration limit on the suspension is shown either way. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).

Personnel actions taken while the suspension was in force are completed acts that the held sources do not tie to the order's continuation; the suspension itself does not survive the revocation.
